evals.name: fix-loop-budget-and-verdict
evals.prompt: The lint is a mess on this branch — a bunch of prettier stuff plus some eslint complaints and I think knip is unhappy about a couple of exports. Can you just clean it all up? Don't spend the whole afternoon on it though.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches qoq-checker (never runs the tools inline), handing it the record's path plus the two paths it cannot derive: the absolute path to scripts/summarize.mjs and the report directory. The checker reads run: and check: from the record as its only read — it never opens the CLI's AGENTS.md, since discovery already distilled the flags into check: — runs `<run:> <check:>` (--json is what writes the reports at all), and calls summarize.mjs with the report dir as its positional argument — never bare. The command fixes findings itself rather than delegating, verifies each fix against the owning tool and then a scoped test:one + build, prints one progress line per loop, stops to ask after 3 loops rather than looping indefinitely, stops without asking if the finding count fails to drop, and ends on a single PASS or FAIL line with the digest underneath.
assertions: Dispatches qoq-checker rather than running the tools inline
Hands the checker the reports-current.mjs path, the summarize.mjs path, and the report directory
Checker branches on reports-current.mjs's exit code (0 reuse, 1 re-run) instead of judging staleness itself
Runs `<run:> <check:>` composed from the record's two lines — never invents the flags, never without --json, and never reads the CLI's AGENTS.md
Calls summarize.mjs with the report dir positionally, never bare
Reads the digest only; does not load a raw report wholesale
The command fixes findings itself rather than dispatching an agent per finding
Each fix is verified by re-running the owning tool, then test:one plus build
A fix that breaks a test is reverted and carried as unfixable, never retried
Prints one progress line per loop showing per-tool before → after counts
Stops and asks after 3 loops rather than looping indefinitely
Stops without asking when a loop fails to reduce the finding count
Ends on a single PASS or FAIL line with the digest underneath

evals.name: refactor-four-assessments-sequential
evals.prompt: src/modules/npm has gotten pretty gnarly — lots of copy-paste and I don't think the shape is right anymore. Give it a proper going over, just that directory.
evals.expected_output: Establishes a green base by dispatching qoq fix scoped to the same path and stops (without asking) if it isn't green. Then runs exactly four assessments strictly in order — JSCPD, project conventions, ponytail-review, design-pattern-review — one at a time and never in parallel, dispatching the two lens skills for 3 and 4. Asks the user per assessment before applying anything, re-greens with qoq fix after each applied assessment, and reports every assessment at the end including empty and declined ones.
assertions: Dispatches qoq fix over the same scope first and refuses to start unless it returns PASS
Stops without asking the user when the base isn't green
Scopes the green base to the requested path, not the whole repo
Runs exactly four assessments in order: JSCPD, project conventions, ponytail-review, design-pattern-review
Runs them one at a time, never in parallel
Dispatches the two lens skills under the names on the record's skills: line
Asks the user per assessment before applying anything, never once up front for all four
Re-dispatches qoq fix after each assessment that applied changes
Reports every assessment at the end, including empty and declined ones
Accepts the scope positionally (no --path flag)

evals.name: blocked-discovery-asks-and-persists
evals.prompt: run qoq fix on this repo
evals.expected_output: Dispatches qoq-discovery, which cannot determine the single-file test command because package.json has both `test:unit` and `test:ci` and no project docs answer it. The agent writes no record at all (not a partial one) and returns the question. The caller asks the user, and once answered writes it into the project's own docs (CLAUDE.md, else AGENTS.md, else README.md) inside a `<!-- qoq:discovery -->` block BEFORE re-dispatching — so a later npm install doesn't cost the same question again. Never guesses a default, and never composes an `npx vitest ...` invocation from package.json dependencies. The caller resolves the two lenses against its own available-skills list and hands the `skills:` line in at dispatch under the exact names that list gives them, plugin prefix included — the agent transcribes it and never searches the filesystem, which cannot see a plugin lens and would record =no for an installed one.
assertions: Dispatches qoq-discovery with the project root and the resolved skills: line — nothing else
The agent writes no record at all when ambiguous — not a partial one
Returns `blocked` with the question rather than guessing a default
Never composes an npx vitest/tsc invocation from package.json dependencies
The caller asks the user rather than picking between test:unit and test:ci
The answer is written into CLAUDE.md, else AGENTS.md, else README.md — never a new file
The answer is written inside a <!-- qoq:discovery --> block
The write happens BEFORE re-dispatching discovery
The caller resolves the lens names from its own available-skills list, plugin prefix included, and passes them in — the agent never derives them from the filesystem
Booleans in the record are written yes/no

evals.name: bump-dirty-tree-hard-stop
evals.prompt: we're way behind on deps, can you update them? I've got a couple of files I'm still working on but they're unrelated, just leave them alone
evals.expected_output: Refuses to start: a clean worktree is an unconditional precondition for bump, because git is what distinguishes a bump's damage from the user's uncommitted work. Says so plainly and tells the user to commit or stash. Does not offer a flag to override, does not proceed on the untouched files only, and does not stash on the user's behalf.
assertions: Refuses to start on a dirty worktree
States that git is what separates a bump's damage from the user's own work
Does not offer a flag or option to override the precondition
Does not proceed on only the untouched files
Does not stash on the user's behalf

evals.name: bump-analyse-then-split-ladder
evals.prompt: worktree is clean. update our npm dependencies — there are a few majors in there I think
evals.expected_output: Analyses first and writes nothing: works out what's outdated, groups minor/patch, plans at most one major step per package, and dispatches one qoq-bumper per major (which reads changelogs and greps this codebase, never edits). Presents the impact and lets the user pick and exclude, and only then writes patches for the chosen set. Applies one patch at a time with reinstall, validates with all three of qoq fix, full test suite, and build after every patch, then runs qoq refactor --decisions auto scoped to that patch's changed files AFTER it validates. A failing grouped patch is reverted and re-cut minor/patch, then per-package, before any package is abandoned.
assertions: The planning phase writes nothing — no tree changes, no patch files
Groups minor and patch bumps and plans at most one major step per package
Dispatches one qoq-bumper per major package
qoq-bumper edits nothing — no source, no package.json, no lockfile
Presents current → target plus the breaking changes that land here, with files
Lets the user pick and exclude before any patch is written
An empty selection is accepted and ends the run
Applies one patch at a time, never a batch
Validates every patch with all three of qoq fix, full test suite, and build
Runs qoq refactor --decisions auto over the patch's changed files AFTER it validates, not before
A failing grouped patch is reverted and re-cut minor/patch, then per package, before any package is abandoned
Passes the refactor scope positionally (no --path flag)

evals.name: plan-criteria-as-assertions
evals.prompt: Here's what we need: users should be able to schedule a report to run daily/weekly, get it emailed as a PDF, and manage their schedules from the settings page. Also rate-limit the schedule creation endpoint. Can you work out how we'd build this?
evals.expected_output: Produces a plan file under ./plans/ following the plan template. Every acceptance criterion is written as an observable assertion a spec could be written from today ("a 6th request inside 60s returns 429"), never as a task ("add rate limiting"). Tickets stop at size M, complexity rates only the model tier (no delivery routing, no per-ticket standards pass), and there are no test-only tickets for feature work. Dispatches Explore for repo patterns but takes build/test commands from the discovery record, not from Explore. Ends at approval and offers qoq execute rather than dispatching any ticket.
assertions: Writes a plan file under ./plans/ named YYYY-MM-DD-<feature>.md
Follows assets/plan-template.md structurally without inventing sections
Every acceptance criterion is an observable assertion, never a task description
No ticket is sized above M
Complexity rates the agent tier only — no delivery routing, no per-ticket standards pass
No test-only tickets for feature work
Dispatches Explore for repo patterns
Takes build and test commands from the discovery record, not from Explore
Saves with Plan status: draft and asks for approval
Surfaces new dependencies and any ticket rated above the session's own model at approval
Offers qoq execute rather than dispatching any ticket itself

evals.name: execute-sequential-tdd-milestone-refactor
evals.prompt: the plan in ./plans/ is signed off — go ahead and build it
evals.expected_output: Loads the plan fresh from disk, checks Plan status is approved, reconciles any in-progress ticket against git log, and asks before working on the default branch. Dispatches ONE qoq-developer at a time in dependency then plan order — no waves, no parallelism flag, no run id — handing it the record's path, the test-conventions.md path, and the ticket's tier explicitly. The developer writes assertions transcribed from the acceptance criteria, implements, raises those assertions to test-conventions.md itself (no `qoq test` dispatch — a subagent can't dispatch), proves the work runs with the project's own test:one and build, and hands back the changed-file list. It never invokes the qoq CLI. THE ORCHESTRATOR then dispatches `qoq fix` scoped to that list — the gate — and commits exactly that ticket's files on PASS; a FAIL re-dispatches the developer with the digest and spends one of its three attempts. The refactor beat runs at the MILESTONE, not per ticket: qoq refactor --decisions auto over the union of the milestone's files plus the full suite and build. Escalates one tier when the budget is spent; never implements anything on the orchestrating thread.
assertions: Loads the plan fresh from disk rather than reusing an in-session copy
Refuses to execute a plan whose status is draft
Reconciles an in-progress ticket against git log rather than asking the user
Asks before dispatching when on the default branch
Dispatches exactly one qoq-developer at a time, in dependency then plan order
No parallel waves and no flag offering them
The dispatch carries the ticket's id, Context, Files and Acceptance criteria verbatim
The dispatch carries the record's path, the test-conventions.md path, and the tier explicitly
The developer writes failing assertions transcribed from the criteria before implementing
The developer raises those assertions to test-conventions.md itself, with no qoq test dispatch
The developer proves its work with the project's own test:one and build
The developer never invokes the qoq CLI
The orchestrator dispatches qoq fix scoped to the returned file list
The commit happens on the orchestrating thread, after PASS, one commit per ticket
A FAIL re-dispatches the developer with the digest and spends one of three attempts
The refactor beat runs at the milestone over the union of its files, not per ticket
The milestone gate also runs the project's full build and test suite
Escalates one tier when the budget is spent, recording the escalation on the ticket
The orchestrating thread never implements anything itself

evals.name: test-red-base-asks-first
evals.prompt: the TokenService in src/auth has no tests at all, can you write some? unit tests are fine
evals.expected_output: Reads runner, globals, react and conventions off the discovery record rather than rediscovering them. States the inferred scope back rather than asking. Runs the full suite BEFORE writing anything to establish a baseline, and on finding pre-existing failures asks the user whether to skip them (recording them as the baseline) or fix them first — it does not silently absorb them into the new work's result. Dispatches qoq-tester one slice at a time, handing over the record path, the test-conventions.md path, the slice, the baseline, and any specs already in place. The tester proves its specs run using only the PROJECT's own scripts — test:one then the full suite against the baseline — never the qoq CLI, and hands back the file list. THE COMMAND then dispatches `qoq fix` scoped to those spec files as the gate, re-running the full suite if fix changed anything, and re-dispatches the tester with the digest on a FAIL. qoq refactor runs ONCE after the last slice, scoped to every file written. Never uses .skip or loosens an assertion to get green.
assertions: Reads runner, globals, react and conventions off the record rather than rediscovering them
States the inferred unit/integration scope back instead of asking
Runs the full suite BEFORE writing anything, to establish a baseline
Asks whether to skip or fix pre-existing failures rather than absorbing them
Dispatches qoq-tester one slice at a time, never two in parallel
The dispatch carries the record path, test-conventions.md path, slice, baseline, and any existing specs
The tester proves its specs with the project's own test:one then the full suite
The tester never invokes the qoq CLI and never edits the code under test
The command dispatches qoq fix over the returned spec files as the gate
Re-runs the full suite when fix changed anything
A FAIL re-dispatches the tester with the digest, spending one of three rewrites
qoq refactor runs ONCE after the last slice, scoped to every file written
Never uses .skip or loosens an assertion to reach green

evals.name: bare-invocation-asks-which-command
evals.expected_output: Six commands are six different jobs and a bare invocation names none of them, so the skill asks which one rather than picking the most likely. Discovery may run first, but no command's work starts before the answer.
assertions: Asks the user which command to run rather than guessing one
Offers the six commands with enough description to choose between them
Does not fix, refactor, bump, plan, execute or test anything before the answer
Does not silently default to fix because it is the most common

evals.name: repaired-record-notified-after-the-work
evals.prompt: run qoq fix over src/auth — I renamed the test script in package.json this morning
evals.expected_output: Discovery finds the recorded test:one no longer resolves, re-derives that line unambiguously and returns `repaired test:one`. The run carries on with the repaired value and the notice reaches the user once the fix loop has reported its verdict — never before it, and never as a request for permission.
assertions: Discovery repairs only the stale line, leaving verified lines untouched
The repair happens in the same dispatch, without asking permission
The run continues with the repaired value rather than stopping
The repair notice is reported AFTER the fix verdict, not before the work
The notice names the field with its old → new value
An ambiguous repair would have been returned as a question instead

evals.name: escalation-exhausted-blocks-the-ticket
evals.prompt: keep going on the plan — ticket 2.3 has already come back failing twice at sonnet
evals.expected_output: The ticket's remaining attempt is spent at its current tier, then it escalates one tier up with the last report and digest pasted into the new prompt. When the top rung is already in use there is nowhere to escalate to: the ticket is marked `blocked`, the report goes to the user, and execution does not quietly continue as though the ticket were done.
assertions: Escalates exactly one tier when the three-attempt budget is spent
The escalated dispatch carries the previous report and digest verbatim
The escalation is recorded on the ticket even if the escalated run passes
At the top tier the ticket is marked blocked rather than retried again
The blocking report reaches the user, distinguishing a bad ticket from too small a model
The ticket is never narrowed and no acceptance criterion is dropped to get past it
A blocked ticket does not stop the milestone's remaining independent tickets

evals.name: compress-default-scope-and-literal-check
evals.prompt: My CLAUDE.md and the AGENTS.md files have gotten really wordy and they're eating my context on every single run. Can you trim them down to just what an agent actually needs?
evals.expected_output: Skips qoq-discovery entirely (nothing on the record describes a markdown file) and says so rather than dispatching it. Resolves the default scope with `git ls-files '*CLAUDE.md' '*AGENTS.md'` and lists what matched before editing anything. Works one file at a time, never in parallel, reading each file whole before cutting. Writes each compressed version to a scratch path first, runs `node <skill>/scripts/compress-check.mjs <original> <scratch>`, and treats a dropped literal as something to restore or justify and an invented one as a hallucinated path to rewrite — never as an automatic revert. Skips files that would save under ~15%. Ends by dispatching `qoq fix` over exactly the changed files so Prettier reformats the markdown, then reports one table of before/after word counts taken from the script's own output, naming every skipped file and every dropped literal it judged redundant.
assertions: Does not dispatch qoq-discovery, and states that compress needs no record
Resolves the default scope with git ls-files over *CLAUDE.md and *AGENTS.md
Lists the matched files before editing any of them
Compresses one file at a time, never dispatching parallel agents
Reads each file whole before cutting anything from it
Writes the compressed version to a scratch path rather than over the original
Runs compress-check.mjs with both the original and the scratch path
Treats a dropped literal as restore-or-justify, not as an automatic revert
Treats an invented literal as a hallucinated path and rewrites
Skips a file whose estimated saving is under roughly 15%, and says why
Keeps every path, command, flag and filename present in the original
Keeps headings stable, or fixes what links to them in the same change
Keeps a rationale clause that prevents a wrong action; cuts one that only justifies a right one
Dispatches qoq fix over exactly the files it changed
Reports a before/after word-count table using the script's own numbers
Edits only markdown — no code, config, or test file is touched
